steps.minor: The minor scale has its own pattern: whole, half, whole, whole, half, whole, whole. From the same note as the major scale, its degrees 3, 6 and 7 are a half step lower. {a} minor uses only white keys, from {a} to the next {a}.
steps.hearScale: Listen to each scale, up from its tonic. The third note tells you: lower and darker in minor.
steps.build: Now build minor scales. The tonic is given: find the rest in order, following the minor pattern.
steps.seventh: Minor melodies often raise degree 7 on the way home, so it sits a half step below the tonic, like {gSharp} in {a} minor. It’s then written with an accidental, because the key signature doesn’t have it.
steps.degrees: Degrees work the same way in minor. Read the note on the staff and count up from the tonic.
